tour.title: Start here — the two binaries
tour.description: CICaDo ships as two Go binaries: a server (control plane with embedded UI) and a runner. Read the CLAUDE.md source-of-truth and the entrypoint binaries to see the system boundaries before diving in.
tour.languageLesson: Go: each cmd/ package is a thin main that wires up server/ or runner/ packages and a frozen gRPC protocol.

tour.title: The frozen runner protocol
tour.description: The cicado/runner/v1 gRPC protocol is the contract between server and runner. It is frozen (additive-changes-only) and drives enrollment, session streams, executors, and the journal that enables reconnect/resume.
tour.languageLesson: Protobuf: services and messages are defined once; Go + generated code is committed under proto/. Behavior changes ride capability flags, never version sniffing.

tour.title: Workflow definition & validation
tour.description: Jobs are declared in repository YAML files. The workflow package owns the schema v1 types, the published JSON Schema, the positional-error YAML parser, DAG `needs` resolution, and trigger/filter/if-conditionals.
tour.languageLesson: Go: schema types + a hand-written parser produce human- and agent-readable positional errors — no external templating engine.

tour.title: The Postgres-backed job queue & scheduler
tour.description: Postgres is the only stateful dependency and also the job queue: leases are claimed via FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and work is woken via LISTEN/NOTIFY. Lease expiry is driven by a sweep.
tour.languageLesson: Go + SQL: the queue and scheduler live in one process; no Redis/SQS/Kafka in the MVP.

tour.title: Data layer — schema & migrations
tour.description: The store/repository layer and goose migrations define the persistence model: orgs, repos, workflows, runs, jobs. The embedded test database mirrors production migrations for the E2E harness.

tour.title: Control plane services
tour.description: Above the queue sit the HTTP API, gRPC runner service, artifacts storage, the audit + event bus, and the log-ingest secret redaction applied before persistence or fan-out.

tour.title: Forge & webhook integration (M3)
tour.description: The Forge adapter interface and the GitHub App webhook receiver bring in external triggers: signature verification, idempotency, and replay tolerance over HTTP.
tour.languageLesson: Go: webhook receiver is server-side only and never runs third-party code in the control plane (ADR-005).

tour.title: Runner agent
tour.description: The runner enrolls, opens the session stream, and executes steps. Reconnection uses full jitter; the journal enables re-execution on resume. Executors include docker and shell.
tour.languageLesson: Go: journal + journal_test pair demonstrates M1 reconnect/resume; lambda is the per-job execution unit.

tour.title: Web UI & deployment
tour.description: The UI is server-rendered (no build step: html/template + embedded FS + htmx). Deployment is a Terraform AWS reference module plus a Docker build and Makefile targets.
tour.languageLesson: No npm/bundler/React — `go build` produces the embedded UI.

tour.title: Testing, docs & decision log
tour.description: The end-to-end harness runs the whole path against a temporary Postgres natively. Documentation is centralized in project-docs; per-tickt decision rationale lives in docs/decisions/ (PR CIC-69).
tour.languageLesson: One PR per Linear ticket; non-trivial decisions are recorded in docs/decisions/CIC-NN-*.md.
